what: AES owns power generation and utilities around the world: regulated utilities in Ohio and Indiana, and renewable and thermal generation in the United States, Latin America and Asia.
customers: Utilities, large corporate buyers signing renewable power contracts, and regulated customers in Ohio and Indiana.
money: wind, solar and storage sold on long-term contracts
regulated electricity in Ohio and Indiana
thermal generation and LNG in several countries
moat: Long-term power purchase agreements with corporate buyers like Microsoft and Amazon, signed before a project is built, which make the revenue contractual rather than market-priced.
risks: Free cash flow is negative by $1.5B because renewable construction spending outruns earnings
Operations across many emerging markets bring currency and political risk
The analyst average target is right where the shares trade
opportunities: 6.0 times earnings and 2.2 times EBITDA, among the lowest valuations in power generation
A contracted renewable backlog signed with data centre operators who need the power
An agreed takeover by Global Infrastructure Partners put a floor under the valuation
watch: The renewable project backlog and progress toward the agreed takeover.
